title: Cashmere stitch spectacle case
subtitle: A spectacle case worked in cashmere stitch on 13-count canvas in two-colour diagonal rows
excerpt: A firm spectacle case worked in cashmere stitch on 13-count canvas. The diagonal rectangular blocks of cashmere stitch run in two alternating colours to create a lattice effect. Finished size is 9 cm wide by 17 cm long, lined with thin felt.
sourceNotes: Cashmere stitch construction from Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Spectacle case format and finishing from Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), needlepoint accessories chapter.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thin inner layer of felt or silk glued or slip-stitched inside a finished needlepoint case to protect the contents from the rough canvas back.

heroPrompt: A finished needlepoint spectacle case in deep blue and grey cashmere stitch diagonal pattern, open to show felt lining, glasses resting beside it, natural light.

content.text: This spectacle case is worked in cashmere stitch on 13-count canvas. Each cashmere block consists of four stitches in a 2 by 3 hole rectangle (short-long-long-short). Two alternating colours produce a diagonal lattice. The case is worked as a single 47 by 88 hole rectangle folded in half, seamed at the sides, and fitted with a felt lining.
What you need

items.label: Canvas
items.value: 13-count mono canvas, cut 20 by 30 cm (leaves a margin around the 47 by 88 hole design area)

items.label: Thread A: main (dark)
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 930 / Anchor 1035 (dark antique blue). About 10 m

items.label: Thread B: contrast (medium)
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 452 / Anchor 232 (medium shell grey). About 10 m

items.label: Felt lining
items.value: Soft felt, one piece 8 by 32 cm

items.label: Sewing thread
items.value: Strong thread in a neutral colour for the side seams

content.text: Palette
Thread A: DMC 930 / Anchor 1035: dark antique blue
Thread B: DMC 452 / Anchor 232: medium shell grey
Stretching the canvas
Mount on a scroll frame. Cashmere stitch runs diagonally and will pull the canvas at an angle. A frame prevents this. The canvas will still benefit from blocking after completion.
Stitches used
Cashmere stitch
: four-stitch rectangular blocks over a 2 by 3 hole area (short stitch over 1, two long stitches over 2, short stitch over 1). Each block is worked diagonally.
Working method
Mark the 47 by 88 hole boundary on the canvas. The fold line runs at hole 44 across the 88-hole length; both halves of the case are the same 47 by 44 hole pattern.
Work cashmere blocks across the canvas in diagonal rows. Place Thread A blocks first across each diagonal, then return to fill the gaps with Thread B blocks.
Complete the full 47 by 88 area. Block by dampening and pinning square to a board overnight.
Finishing

Trim the canvas margin to 1.5 cm. Fold the worked canvas in half along the fold line (hole 44), right side outward. Overcast the two side seams through both layers using strong thread or spare wool. Turn the seam allowances in before sewing. Cut the felt lining to fit inside and slip-stitch it in place to cover the
lining
side.
What to try next
The same case works with a Scotch stitch or Jacquard stitch fill. Use a three-colour palette for a more complex diagonal pattern at the same scale.
